synthesis: Two retrieved records, appraised at abstract level, after a first search that failed and a leads-only reply that could not be assessed. A cluster randomised trial found that offering group care raised attendance at eight or more contacts (71 against 58 percent), especially among women under 20, with less than half of women taking up the offer. A micro-costing study found group care about 12 percent more expensive per woman, driven by rooms, childcare and interpreters and falling with larger groups. No retrieved study combines costs and attendance; the four model leads remain unchecked.
gradeRationale: One randomised trial with deprived areas under-represented and one costing study without outcomes; only two records, indirect to this service.
summary: Two retrieved records appraised; three claims; overall certainty low.
